title: Solar Panels in Mesa, AZ: 2026 Cost, Savings & APS Net Metering Guide
excerpt: Mesa averages 6.5 peak sun hours daily and an APS electricity rate of $0.121/kWh. A 6kW system saves $936/year with a payback period of 10–13 years after incentives.
content:
Mesa Solar Potential: One of America's Best Cities

Mesa, Arizona is the third-largest city in Arizona and one of the top solar cities in the United States with a solar score of 97/100. Situated in the Valley of the Sun, Mesa averages 6.5 peak sun hours per day — nearly 50% more than the US average. With 300+ sunny days per year and low humidity (around 18%), panels in Mesa operate at near-peak efficiency year-round with minimal degradation from weather.

Solar Panel Cost in Mesa, Arizona

A 6 kW residential solar system in Mesa typically costs $15,000–$19,000 before incentives. The 30% federal Investment Tax Credit reduces this by $4,500–$5,700, bringing the net cost to $10,000–$13,500. Arizona does not have a state income tax credit for solar, but does exempt solar systems from the state sales tax (saving $750–$1,200 on a typical system) and from property tax assessment — meaning your home's increased value from solar isn't taxed. Combined with the federal credit, most Mesa homeowners net out at $10,500–$13,000 for a quality 6kW system.

APS Net Metering in Mesa

Most Mesa residents are served by Arizona Public Service (APS). APS's net metering program — called Resource Comparison Proxy (RCP) — credits exported solar energy at a rate slightly below the retail rate. As of 2026, the RCP export credit is approximately $0.076–$0.091/kWh, compared to the retail import rate of $0.121/kWh. This means APS pays you less for what you export than they charge you for what you import — so sizing your system to match your actual consumption (rather than oversizing) is important in Mesa to maximize ROI.

Annual Savings and Payback in Mesa

A properly-sized 6 kW system in Mesa produces approximately 9,855 kWh per year. At APS's retail rate of $0.121/kWh, that's $1,192 in annual electricity savings. After the net cost of $11,000–$13,000, most Mesa homeowners break even in 9–11 years. Over 25 years, total savings reach $25,000–$32,000 accounting for typical APS rate increases of 3–4% per year.

Best Solar Installers in Mesa

Mesa has one of the most competitive solar markets in the US with 100+ licensed installers. Major national companies including Sunrun, SunPower, Tesla Energy, and Palmetto all operate in Mesa. Local Arizona installers like SunHarvest Solar and local affiliates of regional firms often price 10–20% below national brands for comparable equipment. Always get a minimum of 3 quotes — in Mesa's competitive market, quotes for the same system can vary by $3,000–$5,000.

Mesa Solar Timeline

From signed contract to system activation in Mesa typically takes 60–90 days: 1–2 weeks for permits (City of Mesa building permit + APS interconnection application), 1–2 days for installation, and 30–60 days for APS to approve and activate net metering. Some installers offer financing that starts after activation, so you pay nothing during the approval period.
